claims.claim: Weightless neural networks including WiSARD have been experimentally evaluated on network intrusion detection tabular data with time complexity analysis.
claims.quote: evaluate novel datasets (updated w.r.t. the obsolete KDD99 set) through a designed-from-scratch Python-based routine; iii) perform experimental analyses including time complexity and performance

claims.claim: PolyLUT has been demonstrated on network intrusion detection and jet identification tasks which are non-image tabular data.
claims.quote: We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in three tasks: network intrusion detection, jet identification at the CERN Large Hadron Collider, and handwritten digit recognition using the MNIST dataset.

claims.claim: DWN compares favorably against leading approaches for tabular datasets with higher average rank.
claims.quote: DWNs also compare favorably against leading approaches for tabular datasets, with higher average rank.

claims.claim: DWN achieves preferable accuracy to XGBoost on a low-power microcontroller under stringent memory constraints.
claims.quote: a low-power microcontroller, where they achieve preferable accuracy to XGBoost while subject to stringent memory constraints

claims.claim: ULEEN has been compared against BNNs on the four MLPerf Tiny datasets and MNIST.
claims.quote: We compare ULEEN against BNNs in software and hardware using the four MLPerf Tiny datasets and MNIST.

claims.claim: PolyLUT-Add has been evaluated on the Network Intrusion Detection benchmark which is tabular data.
claims.quote: We evaluated our implementation over the MNIST, Jet Substructure classification, and Network Intrusion Detection benchmark

claims.claim: PolyLUT has been demonstrated on network intrusion detection and jet identification tasks.
claims.quote: We demonstrate the effectiveness of PolyLUT on three tasks: network intrusion detection, jet identification at the CERN Large Hadron Collider, and MNIST.

claims.claim: LogicNets, PolyLUT, PolyLUT-Add, and NeuraLUT are existing LUT-DNN approaches that rely on fixed sparsity masks.
claims.quote: existing LUT-DNN approaches (e.g., LogicNets, PolyLUT, PolyLUT-Add, and NeuraLUT) that rely on fixed sparsity masks

claims.claim: SparseLUT training code is publicly available at the specified GitHub repository.
claims.quote: This is done without any hardware overhead and achieves state-of-the-art results for LUT-based DNNs (Code: https://github.com/bingleilou/SparseLUT).

claims.claim: WiSARD, Bloom WiSARD, and BTHOWeN have been evaluated on Bot-IoT, CICIDS, and UNSW-NB15 intrusion-detection tabular datasets.
claims.quote: On the Bot-IoT, CICIDS, and UNSW-NB15 intrusion-detection datasets, adversarial perturbations lead WNN detectors to classify many attacks as normal traffic

claims.claim: DWCs achieve returns competitive with standard deep policies on five MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks.
claims.quote: Across five MuJoCo benchmarks, including high-dimensional Humanoid, DWCs achieve returns competitive with standard deep policies

open_questions: Which of the specific families (WiSARD, BTHOWeN, ULEEN, DWN, LogicNets, PolyLUT) have publicly available open-source implementations?
What are the CPU inference latency and throughput measurements for these families compared to small MLPs on tabular or text data?
Do any of these families have published results on text data (NLP tasks) as opposed to tabular or image data?
How do the inference costs (latency, energy, memory) of these families on CPUs compare quantitatively with small MLPs?
